title: AI-SYS-KPI-03 and AI-SYS-KPI-07 must be exactly 0 and are not baseline-dependent
risk: The two zero-tolerance invariants are treated as targets that may be missed while the baseline is pending, so an authority violation or a duplicate send is filed as a metric miss and the release proceeds.
preconditions: Namespace gov-kpi-<case_id>-<worker_id>; the metric is computed by the real reporting code over fixtures/offline/governance.json kpi_dataset and never copied from the dashboard payload.

Frozen clock 2026-01-15T10:00:00Z with the reporting window 2026-01-01T00:00:00Z .. 2026-02-01T00:00:00Z as a half-open interval; the stored aggregate is recomputed independently from the raw counter rows.
policy_violations and duplicate_executions are both 0 in the synthetic dataset, and the invariant is defined as a hard requirement rather than a target.
A second variant injects one violation row and one duplicate effect so the case proves a non-zero value blocks the release instead of being reported.

steps.action: Read the two invariants from the dataset
steps.expected: Both are reported as exactly 0 and the report states that zero is required, not a target that may be missed.

steps.action: Inject one violation row and one duplicate effect and re-evaluate
steps.expected: Both metrics become non-zero and the run reports a release-blocking error; no ASM-002 exemption is applied and no threshold is consulted.

steps.action: Compare with the two monitoring metrics
steps.expected: Hallucination/Error Rate and Failed Execution are reported as measured values with their proposed design targets explicitly labelled as unapproved, so they are not mistaken for pass/fail bars.

steps.action: Attempt to weaken the invariants via the assumption registry
steps.expected: The attempt is refused: ASM-002 cannot loosen a safety invariant, and an unlocked KPI baseline does not convert the invariant into a measurable target.

assertions: Policy Violation Rate and Duplicate Execution are exactly 0 in the accepted run, and any non-zero value is a release-blocking error rather than a metric miss.
The two invariants are independent of the ASM-002 baseline: an unlocked baseline cannot relax, weight or defer them.
The monitoring metrics are visibly separated from the invariants and their proposed thresholds are labelled as unapproved design targets.
A blocked violation attempt still counts in the invariant numerator, so a control that fires is not evidence of a clean record.
forbidden: Reporting the invariants as targets that may be missed.
Applying an ASM-002 exemption to an authority violation or a duplicate send.
Excluding a violation because execution was blocked before it took effect.
evidence: Invariant evaluation rows for both metrics with the fixture values.
Release-blocking error record from the injected variant with the offending row ids.
Monitoring metric report showing the unapproved threshold labels.
cleanup: Delete gov- evaluation rows and the injected variant rows after export.
automation: The reporting service and the metric dictionary run as real code under test over the frozen KPI dataset; the dashboard is a consumer whose displayed value must equal the independently recomputed value. Waits are condition-based on the stored aggregate row, metric values are never supplied as inputs, and no vendor boundary is involved in the arithmetic.
prerequisites: ASM-002 is unlocked, which affects targets only: the two zero-tolerance invariants remain hard requirements and must be evaluated regardless of the baseline.
